- File: .github/workflows/clarify.yml
  Line or code reference: lines 425-428 (LAST RUN DIFF hunk)
  Problem: The inline `gh_retry_to_file` fallback function is defined inside the `if ! type ...` block. The `local out="$1"; shift; local attempt=1` declarations sit inside a function body that bash only parses at call time, so they remain dormant until the first invocation; the warning line and the function definition are the two commands actually executed by `then`. The function persists for the rest of the step's bash, and the next call (`gh_retry_to_file "${RESUME_COMMENTS_FILE}.pages" gh api --paginate ...`) uses it. The retry/backoff math and `return` paths behave as intended, but there is no per-call progress log — only the one warning at definition time — so a degraded run that exhausts retries is only visible through the outer `::warning::final_merge_resume check failed for closed issue #N`.
  Why it fails at runtime: It does not actually fail. The fallback works, but the absence of a per-retry log makes a degraded-but-recovered run indistinguishable from a first-attempt success.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2
